title: Review: adversarial Opus 5.5 pass over the S44 repair (eighth)
description: Read-only adversarial review of PR #599 commits cf53c7c1 + 06cbb44f (merge 50da5092) against 7414d014: the S44 repair (spec in eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.17). Governing hard rule (bd memory srd-fidelity-hard-blocker): any engine behaviour contradicting the SRD in letter or spirit is a blocker. Attack: 'absent' status semantics and every status consumer (turns, action economy, concentration, usage counters, projection/actor sync, combat close, recovery clock, admission/new manifestation); zero_hp_rule derivation from records (all 11 zero-hit-points records, incl. Simulacrum, Animate Objects, Giant Insect) and every route to 0 HP; link closing and effect end on last vanish (cascades, re-entry, events, terminal invariants); guards making dying/stable under remove unreachable (all orders and paths, incl. campaign_actor links, re-bound links after combat close, replacement concentration); F3 remove seam (no translation of remove into release; missing only when truly unreachable); record-derived cleanup policies vs source text for each conjure spell; migration 0039 fidelity vs 0033-0038; model-facing tool descriptions/results and docs truthful vs code. Known scope exclusions: eshyra-ysr3 (revert runtime), eshyra-7vh3 (+1 h cast-anchored removal).
acceptance_criteria: Findings recorded in bd notes in S-numbered format (S45+), each with authority, boundary, reachable scenario through the tool registry, sibling analysis, minimal repair, permanent evidence; overall disposition; no file changes; bead closed by the reviewer.
notes:
EIGHTH PASS (adversarial Opus 5.5, S44 repair), bound to head 50da5092, diff 7414d014..50da5092 (cf53c7c1 + 06cbb44f). Read-only; probes are scratch vitest files outside the worktree that drive createDefaultToolRegistry().invoke (same harness as zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy.test.ts). Worktree left clean.

S45 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:3333-3343 (owner exception for priorConcentration) + 3446-3465 (replacement finalizeEnd runs AFTER actor validation) + 3612-3627 (actor link insert); the new absent refusal at activeEffects.ts:1752-1758 runs before the replacement end and is bypassed.
Authority: S44 repair spec A (eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.17: "a combatant that is absent is not a participant"; absent is terminal on the row) and its completion note ("absent refuses ... new effect participation"); SRD spell:conjure-animals ("disappears ... when the spell ends") with rule:concentration (casting another concentration spell ends the first); ADR 0020 state integrity; review policy (truthful model-facing results).
Reachable scenario (registry, fresh): start_encounter wiz + b1; start_effect e1 spell:conjure-animals concentrationOwner c-wiz actors [c-b1]; start_effect e2 spell:conjure-animals (same owner) actors [c-b1] (a plausible "recast to refresh" with reused ids). Result: OK. e1 ends concentration-broken:new-concentration, its remove cleanup makes c-b1 'absent' (SRD-correct), then e2 inserts an ACTIVE actor link (remove/remove) over the absent c-b1 in the same transaction. e2 is a live concentration summoning effect whose only creature is out of play; its result lists the link as active; damage to c-b1 is refused (absent); ending e2 later reports 'removed' again for a creature that left play under e1. The refusal requireParticipant added for absent creatures is thereby bypassed, and the summon the model believes e2 created never appears.
Sibling analysis: (a) condition links of a replacement effect on a creature the prior cleanup removes fail closed (start_effect refused, rolled back) but with a message claiming the still-alive creature is absent - same ordering root; (b) Conjure Elemental/Fey (break=release): the replacement legitimately keeps the creature present (released), and relinking it is pre-existing S1 behaviour - not promoted; (c) effect targets/source actor: same validate-before-replace ordering. No other path creates a link over an absent holder (requireParticipant covers start_effect; close-combat rebind only touches active links).
Minimal repair: after the priorConcentration finalizeEnd, re-check every actor (and condition/target) participant for status 'absent' and refuse with a message naming the cause (the prior spell's creatures disappeared when its concentration ended; summon new combatants) - or refuse up front any actor whose active link belongs to priorConcentration with cleanup_on_break 'remove'.
Permanent evidence: one row in zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy.test.ts 'F3 remove policy' block: replacement Conjure Animals relinking the prior effect's beast is refused and leaves e1 active/beast alive (transaction rolled back); Conjure Elemental relink row stays allowed.

S46 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:3051-3062 (setStatus applied after the damage event) with combatantLifecycle.ts:182-205 (absent branch refusal text)
Authority: review policy (model-facing errors truthful); update_combatant contract (an hpDelta to 0 with status is the documented monster pattern, and the description says a vanish creature "becomes absent when hpDelta brings it to 0 hit points"); ADR 0020 (the engine, not the model, owns the outcome).
Reachable scenario (registry, fresh): Conjure Animals beast c-b1 7/7 linked; update_combatant {combatantId:'c-b1', hpDelta:-10, status:'dead'} (also 'escaped', 'inactive', 'alive') => ERR "an absent combatant cannot change status"; c-b1 is still alive 7/7 (rolled back). The error asserts a state that does not exist; a model following it narrates the beast as vanished while it keeps 7 HP and its turns (state divergence). On 7414d014 the same call killed the beast; the 'lethal damage + status dead' form is a common model idiom.
Sibling analysis: status 'unconscious'/'stable' with damage is caught earlier by the explicit knockout refusal (correct message); set_suffocation/adjust_exhaustion carry no status and vanish correctly (probed); setStatus alone on an alive vanish creature is unaffected.
Minimal repair: in updateCombatantInTxn, when the damage/clamp transition yields 'absent' from a non-absent state and input.status is present, either treat status 'dead' as redundant (the vanish outcome wins) or refuse up front with a precise message ("its spell says it disappears at 0 hit points; pass hpDelta without status"). Do not let the generic absent-row refusal speak for a row that is not absent.
Permanent evidence: extend the existing 'zero-hit-point vanish' describe with a parameterised row (status dead/escaped/inactive with lethal hpDelta) asserting the chosen outcome and, if refused, that the message does not claim the creature is absent and the row is unchanged.

S47 | blocker (SRD hard rule) | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:1905-1916 (admission refusal only covers an existing dead/dying/stable actor) and 1953-1985/2014-2016 (upsert + projection status 'dead' at 0 HP); invariant I11 at encounterCombatants.ts:766-776 and combatantLifecycle.ts:812-822 explicitly tolerates a 'vanish' creature that is 'dead' at 0 HP
Authority: SRD spell:find-familiar / spell:find-steed ("When the familiar drops to 0 hit points, it disappears, leaving behind no physical form"), spell:conjure-* ("disappears when it drops to 0 hit points"), spell:simulacrum ("reverts to snow and melts instantly"); records' zero-hit-points transitions (presence->absent / integrity->destroyed); S44 spec B ("every event that brings HP from >0 to 0 ... yields absent instead of dead/dying/stable/unconscious"; out-of-combat HP to 0 applies the same outcome); docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md:405-410 ("reaching 0 HP by any route ... never dead").
Reachable scenario (registry, fresh): start_effect ruling Find Familiar actors [{combatantId:'c-b1', atZeroHitPoints:'vanish'}] (until-removed); close_combat_instance -> link rebound to campaign actor b1, actor alive 7/7 with combatLifecycle.zeroHpRule 'vanish'; start_encounter c2 actors [{actorId:'b1', hpCurrent:0, status:'dead'}] => OK: actor b1 'dead' 0/7, projection c2-b1 'dead' 0/7 zeroHpRule 'vanish', link still active, effect active. The familiar dropped to 0 HP and left a corpse - the exact outcome the SRD text forbids; for Find Familiar/Find Steed/Simulacrum (no spell-end removal) the corpse persists indefinitely. The same admission without status ({hpCurrent:0}) is refused by I11, so only the 'dead' spelling slips through. Admission is the only model-reachable out-of-combat HP write (updateCampaignActor has no tool), so this is the model's path for "it was killed between scenes".
Sibling analysis: in-combat routes (damage, exhaustion clamp, suffocation) vanish correctly and lethal damage + status dead is refused (S46); start_effect linking an already-dead 0-HP combatant under vanish is allowed (activeEffects.ts:3262-3270) - that creature died before it was summoned, not by its own 0-HP rule, so not promoted; status 'dead' with HP above 0 (instant death without 0 HP) stays dead until the spell ends - SRD-consistent, not promoted.
Minimal repair: in startEncounterInTxn, for an existing non-dead actor whose combatLifecycle.zeroHpRule is 'vanish', supplied hpCurrent 0 must either refuse with the vanish message regardless of status, or apply the vanish outcome (actor absent via absentActorState + closeActorLinkAtZeroHp, not projected); then tighten I11 so 'dead' at 0 HP is accepted for a vanish creature only when the row was already dead before the rule applied.
Permanent evidence: one parameterised row in zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy.test.ts 'absent' block: rebound vanish summon admitted with {hpCurrent:0} and {hpCurrent:0,status:'dead'} => never dead (refused or absent), link closed iff absent.

Checked and found correct (fresh registry probes): Conjure Animals per-beast vanish, link removed(zero-hit-points), last beast ends effect source-removed; Conjure Elemental omitted policies derive remove/release, explicit contradictions refused with record text (CE break 'remove', CA break 'release'); released elemental keeps zeroHpRule, PC opt-in and knockout refused, damage to 0 => absent with effectId null; exhaustion clamp to 0 (hpMax 1, level 4) and suffocation drop vanish; exhaustion level 6 stays dead, end_effect then dead->absent (I8 amended); combat close with combatant-owned concentration removes campaign-actor beasts to absent (closure runs before the instance flip, so no false 'missing'); ruling vanish summon survives close, rebinds, re-projects with zeroHpRule, PC opt-in refused via the rebound campaign_actor link, vanish closes the rebound link and ends the effect; end_effect with no projection => actor absent via removeCampaignActorFromPlay; re-admission without hp refused, with hp starts alive with fresh lifecycle (zeroHpRule null, conditions reset), also from a vanished 0-HP actor; Simulacrum vanish breaks its own concentration and cascades (owned Conjure Animals beast removed); self-concentrating summon vanish; absent refuses record_death_save, set_suffocation, adjust_exhaustion, damage/heal/conditions/status, usage counters, action economy, new participation; location/placement writes still allowed (harmless); migration 0039 constraints/indexes match 0033-0038 plus 'absent' and zero_hp_rule, snapshot consistent; record derivation over all 11 zero-hit-points records (Animate Objects/Giant Insect 'revert' feed guards only, eshyra-ysr3 excluded). Observation, no requirement: condition links on an absent creature report 'missing' at cleanup and the stale condition is discarded on re-manifestation. Observation outside this diff: spell:unseen-servant ("If it drops to 0 hit points, the spell ends") has no mechanics transitions, so derivation cannot cover it; atZeroHitPoints 'vanish' is the available declaration - importer follow-up, not this PR.

DISPOSITION: CHANGES REQUESTED (S47 blocker under the SRD hard rule; S45, S46 should-fix).
